label: Grounded the Capabilities Approach in Aristotelian human functioning and flourishing
description: Martha Nussbaum developed her Neo-Aristotelian Capabilities Approach by translating Aristotle's ergon (human functioning) and civic eudaimonia into universal constitutional entitlements across cultures.
dialecticalTension: Transforms ancient polis-centered virtue politics into universalist cosmopolitan social justice.
historicalContext: Formulated from The Fragility of Goodness (1986) through Women and Human Development (2000).

citations.author: Martha Nussbaum
citations.work: Women and Human Development: The Capabilities Approach

label: Reworked Stoic cognitive theory of emotions alongside tragic vulnerability
description: In The Therapy of Desire (1994) and Upheavals of Thought (2001), Nussbaum adopted the Stoic insight that emotions are evaluative value judgments while rejecting Stoic detachment in favor of Aristotelian vulnerability.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes Stoic cognitive appraisal of emotions with Aristotelian openness to attachment and grief.
historicalContext: Contemporary revival of Hellenistic moral psychology in analytic philosophy.

citations.author: Martha Nussbaum

label: Advanced neo-Aristotelian ethical naturalism into global political justice
description: Building on Foot's Natural Goodness and neo-Aristotelian species-flourishing, Nussbaum extended human-capabilities naturalism into international development ethics and constitutional law.
dialecticalTension: Bridges Oxford virtue naturalism with Rawlsian political liberalism.

citations.author: Ingrid Robeyns and Morten Fibieger Byskov

label: Critiqued Rawlsian contractarianism for excluding disability, global justice, and animals
description: While deeply indebted to Rawls's political liberalism, Nussbaum argued in Frontiers of Justice (2006) that social contract models built on mutual advantage among roughly equal adults fail to secure justice for disabled people, poor nations, and non-human animals.
dialecticalTension: Replaces procedural contractarian reciprocity with substantive threshold capabilities.
historicalContext: Major post-Rawlsian debate in contemporary political philosophy (2006).

citations.author: Martha Nussbaum
citations.work: Frontiers of Justice: Disability, Nationality, Species Membership

label: Systematized the ten central human capabilities as constitutional justice thresholds
description: Nussbaum articulated ten central capabilities—from bodily integrity and practical reason to affiliation and political control—as non-negotiable minimum entitlements for human dignity.
dialecticalTension: Operationalizes flourishing as measurable substantive freedoms rather than utilitarian preference satisfaction.
historicalContext: Developed in Women and Human Development (2000) and Creating Capabilities (2011).
